description: Preview the message a draft would send right now, or at `sendAt`: sender, recipient, subject, attached `files` and the bodies with the signature added, plus anything that would keep it from going (a suppressed recipient, a paused mailbox, a daily cap or the plan's daily sends used up) and `warnings` (`files_on_first_email` when a draft with attached files goes to an address that has not written to the workspace). `recipient` says where the address stands: a new message needs a fresh address check, and a reply to mail you received needs none (`recipient` is null). The blockers `recipient_invalid`, `recipient_not_checked` and `recipient_needs_review` say what the check found; send_draft with `recipientReviewed: true` lifts only the last. `files_not_from_our_servers` means the draft has attached files and its mailbox sends through our mail servers; `message_too_large` means the message and its attached files exceed the mailbox's size limit. `unfilled_merge_fields` means a merge field such as `{{ company }}` is still in the text (`unfilled` lists them): nothing fills it in when a draft is sent, so write the words in its place. One a reply's subject kept from the message it answers is that sender's text and never counts. Nothing is reserved or counted. For a new message or a reply to your own sent mail, `mailbox_resting` names a health or cold guardrail rest, and `mailbox_domain_failing` names domain records past their grace. `usage.mailboxDay.limit` is the cold ceiling scaled by health, at most the mailbox's daily cap. A reply to mail received keeps the ordinary cap and gets none of these cold blockers.

sendAt.description: The moment you plan to send it, as an ISO 8601 date and time with its offset. The preview then says what that send would meet: an address check still running doesn't stop it, and `recipient.expiresBeforeSend` warns when the address's check goes out of date first. Left out, or already past, it previews a send now. In a URL, write the offset's `+` as `%2B`; a space in its place, which is what an unescaped `+` becomes, is read as `+`.

name: preview_draft
title: Preview a draft
